evals.prompt: I put a talk's chapters into an Opus file with ffmpeg (-i talk.wav -i talk.ffmeta -map 0:a -map_metadata 1 -map_chapters 1 -c:a libopus). Its chapters start at 0, 0:10.25 and 1:02.75; the first two are right, but the third now starts at 1:03.75. Why, and how do I fix it?
evals.expected_output: ffmpeg writes a Vorbis chapter's time with its whole seconds rounded, not truncated (vorbiscomment.c): a start half a second or more past a second comes out a second late, so 62.75 s becomes CHAPTER002=00:01:03.750 while 10.25 s stays right. Write the comments from whole milliseconds by division -- ffmeta, or ffman convert --metadata talk.ffmeta. Run: ffmpeg's chapters at 0, 10.25 and 63.75 s; ffman's at 0, 10.25 and 62.75 s.

evals.prompt: Turn these Vorbis comments into a cue sheet for notes.flac: ALBUM=Field Notes, ARTIST=Ana Lima, GENRE=Spoken Word, DATE=2024, and chapters Prologue at 00:00:00.000, Part "One" at 00:07:41.010, Part Two at 00:19:02.400.
evals.expected_output: Disc TITLE "Field Notes"; REM GENRE "Spoken Word" quoted (a space), REM DATE 2024 unquoted; ARTIST has no cue field (only ALBUMARTIST is the disc PERFORMER): stated lost; FILE "notes.flac" WAVE; tracks 01-03 AUDIO, INDEX 01 at 00:00:00, 07:41:01 (461.010 s to the nearest frame, 34,576: 3.33 ms late) and 19:02:30 (exact); track 2's title holds a quote, which no cue string can: dropped and stated. Run: libcue reads the disc's TITLE, GENRE and DATE and tracks at frames 0, 34576 and 85680; metaflac's block, read by ffmpeg, gives chapters at 0, 461.013 and 1142.4 s.

evals.prompt: My string quartet rip's cue sheet has REM DISCID 7A0B1C09, REM REPLAYGAIN_ALBUM_GAIN -4.10 dB, a disc TITLE, PERFORMER and SONGWRITER, a REM REPLAYGAIN_TRACK_GAIN on track 1 and a PERFORMER on track 2. What survives as the single FLAC's Vorbis comments, and what in an ffmetadata file instead?
evals.expected_output: Both: the disc PERFORMER as the album artist (ALBUMARTIST, album_artist), TITLE as the album, REPLAYGAIN_ALBUM_GAIN whole (-4.10 dB); SONGWRITER and REM DISCID lost (none maps them; DISCID is CDDB's). Vorbis also loses track 1's gain and track 2's PERFORMER -- a Vorbis chapter holds a title and a URL alone -- while ffmetadata keeps them as chapter tags (REPLAYGAIN_TRACK_GAIN, performer). Run: ffmeta's outputs and notes as stated for both targets.
